title: ow says /oh/
parentNote: ow says /oh/ — snow, row, blow, grow. It is the same sound as yesterday's oa, and the two of them split the job between them in a way that is worth pointing out: oa sits in the middle of a word, ow sits on the end. boat and road, but snow and blow. That covers nearly everything your child will meet for a long while. The slip to expect is the w, which is not really doing a w job here at all — it is part of the team, so blow is not bl-oh-wuh. Cover the w, say the o, then uncover it and say the whole word once. One warning for later: ow is a letter pair that will turn up much further on saying something completely different. It does not today, and every word in this lesson is the /oh/ kind, so if your child reads one of them the other way, just say the word yourself and move on.

activities.mouthCue: The same round mouth as yesterday: lips forward into an o, then closing a little, like saying oh.
activities.prompt: Two letters, one sound, and it is the sound we did yesterday. The w is part of the team and does not speak on its own: ow.
Three things an o can be part of. Find the team that says the letter name.
Three vowel teams, three different letter names. Which one is today's?
Two sounds. Say the r, then the team, and do not let the w speak on its own.
Here the team comes first, and there is still a sound after it. That happens, but not often.
The long one, and it has two teams in it. ai in the middle, ow on the end.
All three end with the team. The two sounds at the front are the whole difference.
One of these has no team in it. Listen for a long sound at the front, and then to the end.
This one is hard. Three words, all with the team, and only the first sounds to tell them apart.

activities.title: The crow and the snowman
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Snow fell in the dark, and in the sun it did glow.
Meg and I did run to the grass and did make a snowman.
It did grow and grow. It is big, and it is fat.
I did set a red hat on top and did stick an oak arm in it.
Then a crow did land on the hat and did croak at us.
Flap, flap. It did grab the red hat and did flap off to the oak.
Meg did wail. The snowman did not own a hat.
But the sun did glow hot, and the snow did drip and drip.
The snowman did get low, and then it did melt in a wet heap.
The crow did throw the hat back on the grass. It did want a snowman, not just a hat.
